family.description: Methanococcus jannaschii contains homologues of most genes required for spermidine polyamine biosynthesis. Yet genomes from neither this organism nor any other euryarchaeon have orthologues of the pyridoxal 5'-phosphate- dependent ornithine or arginine decarboxylase genes, required to produce putrescine. Instead,these organisms have a new class of arginine decarboxylase (PvlArgDC) formed by the self-cleavage of a proenzyme into a 5-kDa subunit and a 12-kDa subunit that contains a reactive pyruvoyl group. Although this extremely thermostable enzyme has no significant sequence similarity to previously characterised proteins, conserved active site residues are similar to those of the pyruvoyl-dependent histidine decarboxylase enzyme, and its subunits form a similar (alpha-beta)(3) complex. Homologues of PvlArgDC are found in several bacterial genomes, including those of Chlamydia spp., which have no agmatine ureohydrolase enzyme to convert agmatine (decarboxylated arginine) into putrescine. In these intracellular pathogens, PvlArgDC may function analogously to pyruvoyl-dependent histidine decarboxylase; the cells are proposed to import arginine and export agmatine, increasing the pH and affecting the host cell's metabolism. Phylogenetic analysis of Pvl- ArgDC proteins suggests that this gene has been recruited from the euryarchaeal polyamine biosynthetic pathway to function as a degradative enzyme in bacteria [[cite:PUB00027451]].
family.name: Pyruvoyl-dependent arginine decarboxylase (PvlArgDC)

causal_graphs.context: pPRDC.19 mutant derivatives expressed in E. coli B834(DE3), N-terminal His tag removed. Assay at 343 K for 30 min: 50 mM MES/NaOH pH 6.0, 50 mM KCl, 1 mM DTT, 4 mM L-arginine plus 2 ul radiolabeled L-arginine; HCl termination and 14CO2 scintillation measurement.

evidence.explanation: Table 2 WT row and Methods 2.5 define the measured CO2 endpoint; source and preparation limitations are retained.

edges.mechanism: The enzyme/substrate preparation releases 14CO2; the WT comparator has reported specific activity 1014 +/-58 pmol/min/ug. This readout is not direct measurement of every intermediate or an intracellular flux.
edges.subject: wt-arginine-assay

evidence.explanation: Table 2 and Results 3.1/3.3 support the preparation-level decrease, not direct proof of Glu109 proton donation or a measured processing rate.

edges.mechanism: E109Q gives 132 +/-8 versus WT 1014 +/-58 pmol/min/ug, approximately 7.7-fold lower with about 13% residual activity. Separate E109Q crystals are fully processed and contain agmatine; the mutation is not a processing or catalytic null.
edges.subject: e109q-preparation

evidence.explanation: Table 2 and Results 3.3; nonzero residual activity and unresolved processing contribution qualify the effect.

edges.mechanism: N47A gives 2 versus WT 1014 +/-58 pmol/min/ug, roughly 500-fold lower. Table 2 supplies no N47A uncertainty. The measured decrease does not distinguish impaired catalytic chemistry from altered maturation or active-site abundance.
edges.subject: n47a-preparation

causal_graphs.family_mapping: MJ0316/pdaD, Q57764 sequence version 1 exactly equals AAB98302.1, 165 aa; JAL-1/DSM 2661 reference taxon 243232. PF01862 19-162 includes N47 and E109. Published primers and PDB 2QQC/2QQD confirm the substitutions; residual His0 is not included in native numbering. No isolated-domain sufficiency.
causal_graphs.limitations: DIRECT denotes net purified-preparation effects, not proton transfer or a measured self-processing rate. Specific activity per protein mass is not kcat per processed site. WT assay-preparation details, replicate count, uncertainty definition, blank subtraction and tracer specific activity were not independently established. Mutant processing/folding differences can contribute; neither mutant is inactive.

causal_graphs.context: Crystals grown at 295 K with 1-2 mM arginine in PEG2000/MPD/glycerol and HEPES pH 6.7-7.3; assay instead at 343 K and pH 6.0. A failed processing comparison at 338 K for 3 h supplied no relative WT/mutant rate.

evidence.explanation: Methods 2.5, Results 3.1-3.3, Conclusions and inspected Figures 3/4 support a stated mechanistic hypothesis; no observed rate or quantitative mediation is assigned.
evidence.snippet: Efforts to measure the rate of autoprocessing were inconclusive

edges.mechanism: An unprocessed fraction could reduce the abundance of catalytically mature sites per unit protein and contribute to the observed activity loss. Mixed crystal states and altered local contacts motivate this explanation; they do not demonstrate the intervening change in assay solution or exclude impaired turnover of the processed fraction.
edges.subject: reduced-mature-active-fraction

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Intact Q57764/AAB98302.1 N47A, PF01862 19-162; cleavage is between native S52 and S53, yielding the S53-derived pyruvoyl group. PDB 2QQD includes processed and unprocessed chains plus residual His0. This is not a claim for all PF01862 members.
causal_graphs.limitations: Crystal populations are not assay-solution processing fractions. One N47A site is mixed and modeled predominantly processed; four are unprocessed and one clearly processed. N47A local structural comparison uses S53A, not WT. Processing-rate comparison was inconclusive, and neither molecular mediation nor its quantitative contribution was established.

evidence.explanation: E109Q retains activity and fully processed crystal protomers; N47A retains low activity with mixed processing states. Neither establishes a unique catalytic chemical step.

discussions.notes: See evidence/PF01862/PvlArgDC-identity.txt and pvlargdc-gap-ledger.txt. Obtain matched assay-solution processing fractions, valid WT processing controls, activity per processed site and folding controls. Do not treat PYR53 deposit metadata labeled expression tag as biological identity.
discussions.prompt: Quantify maturation separately from catalytic activity of processed sites.
discussions.rationale: Mutant preparation activities and crystal states support distinct observations. The published failed processing-rate comparison cannot establish relative maturation kinetics or mediation of N47A activity loss.

evidence.explanation: Original biochemical characterization and proposed bacterial host effects need separate primary assessment; no host-pH edge adopted.
TK0149 activity and agmatine-dependent deletion growth are leads; exact strain, dose, medium and rescue context remain unverified.

discussions.notes: Keep IN_PROGRESS. Do not transfer PLP-dependent ADC mechanisms, BpsA phenotypes or whole-family essentiality. Graph count is not completion and the hypothetical processing contribution is not an observed biochemical step.
